item.title: Agric ministry puts post-harvest loss at $10bn yearly
item.description: •As 14 of 17 federal silos fail •20% of grains, 70% of fruits, vegetables lost By Gabriel Ewepu ABUJA — THE Minister of Agriculture and Food Security, Senator Abubakar Kyari, Tuesday, disclosed that Nigeria loses an estimated $10 billion annually to post-harvest losses. Kyari made this known as one of the panelists focusing on the topic ‘Productivity Revolution for Growth’ at the ongoing 32nd Nigerian Economic Summit (NES#32) organised by the Nigerian Economic Summit Group, NESG, in Abuja. He also said Nigeria loses between 15 and 20 per cent of its grains, including rice, maize and millet, while losses involving tomatoes, pepper, onions, fruits and vegetables could reach 60 to 70 per cent, depending on the season. He described the reduction of post-harvest losses as a low-hanging fruit in Nigeria’s food security drive, said the country could significantly improve food availability and farmers’ earnings by addressing weaknesses in storage, processing, transportation and market infrastructure. He stated: “We lose almost about $10 billion annually on post-harvest losses. “About 15 to 20 per cent on grains, and you can see grains that are hard, and you probably think we will not lose much of that, but we lose on grains, on cereal, rice, maize, and so on and so forth, millet. On fruits and vegetables, the minister warned that the scale of waste was considerably higher. “Tomato, pepper, onion, and other fruits and vegetables, we lose some of that as high as 60 to 70 per cent depending on the season”, Kyari said, attributing the vulnerability of tomatoes, in particular, to their short shelf life and the effects of hot weather. The Minister also lamented that 17 of the 33 silo complexes built by the Federal Government had been concessioned to private operators, but only three were performing. “The government had concessioned 17 out of the 33 silos that it had built over a period of time, but I’ll tell you that out of the 17, only three have performed. All the 14 are almost comatose for the past, I believe, since when it was concessioned”, he said. The minister attributed the problem partly to a disconnect between agricultural production centres and the location of storage facilities. According to him, some farming communities are situated more than 100 kilometres from major storage facilities, making it difficult and costly for farmers to transport their produce to the silos. He argued that the country’s storage strategy must be redesigned to reflect the geographical distribution of agricultural production rather than depend exclusively on large-scale facilities located far from farming communities. The minister’s position suggests that the challenge extends beyond the physical availability of silos to questions of accessibility, operational efficiency, commercial viability and the suitability of infrastructure to the needs of farmers. item.title: Miners’ deaths: Panel recommends summary dismissal, prosecution of NSCDC officers, N1.4bn for victims
item.description: •Says overcrowding, heat stress, dehydration caused deaths •Rules out use of chemicals; as FG vows justice By Omeiza Ajayi ABUJA—An independent ministerial committee has recommended summary dismissal, administrative sanctions and prosecution of some officers of the Nigerian Security and Civil Defence Corps, NSCDC, over the deaths of 33 detainees in the custody of its Niger State command in Minna, along with N1.4 billion in compensation for victims and survivors. The committee’s chairman, Jonathan Kure, who presented the report to the Minister of Interior, Olubunmi Tunji-Ojo, in Abuja, yesterday, described the deaths as “entirely preventable.” Kure said the committee concluded that the incident was a preventable custodial tragedy, caused by severe overcrowding, unlawful and unsuitable detention conditions, failure of duty of care, disregard of repeated distress warnings, inadequate supervision, and wider systemic deficiencies. He said the evidence did not support claims that the deaths resulted from a disease outbreak. According to him, “available medical and forensic evidence instead indicated that the fatalities resulted from an environmental asphyxia, an acute respiratory failure caused by prolonged confinement in a severely overcrowded and poorly ventilated detention cell, aggravated by heat stress and dehydration.” The 65-page report, of which 46 pages form the main body, examined the arrest, detention, treatment and deaths of detainees between September 15 and 17, 2026. It was commissioned by the minister, following a presidential directive. The committee said the tragedy stemmed from enforcement operations against suspected illegal mining in and around Minna. No headquarter’s approval Kure said: “The operation was undertaken without an approved operational order, proper planning and consultation with relevant mining authorities, or involvement of the specialised Mining Marshals unit. National headquarters was not informed before the operation commenced,” he added. He said the raids led to the arrest of men, women and children, and that by the evening of September 16, 75 persons had been detained. He said after one release, 74 remained in custody overnight, with about 50 male detainees confined in a cell measuring about 20 square metres. The committee said the cell had “a solid metal door, inadequate airflow, no running water, poor lighting, and no functioning toilet.” It said food and drinking water were either unavailable or grossly inadequate, adding that adults and minors were held together. It found that the conditions breached constitutional safeguards, the Administration of Criminal Justice Act, the Child Rights Act and accepted international standards. item.title: FG, NLC reach deal on N70,000 transport allowance, 19-month health workers’ arrears
item.description: By Victor Ahiuma-Young The Federal Government and the Nigeria Labour Congress, NLC, have reached an agreement on a series of measures to ease the economic difficulties facing workers, including a ₦70,000 transport intervention and the payment of 19 months’ arrears owed health workers. The resolutions were reached at a conciliation meeting held at the Federal Ministry of Labour and Employment yesterday, following an earlier meeting convened on October 22. The meetings were organised to address concerns raised by the NLC over the rising cost of living, the implementation of the National Minimum Wage, petroleum pump prices, workers’ welfare and outstanding allowances. The agreement was signed on behalf of the federal government by Dr. Muhammad Maigari Dingyadi, Minister of Labour and Employment; Timi Yakubu, Director-General, Budget; and Dr. Garba Abdul S. U., Permanent Secretary (SWO), Office of the Head of the Civil Service of the Federation, while NLC president, Joe Ajaero, and National Secretary, JNPSNC, Olowoyo Gbenga, stood for labour. Under the agreement, the federal government will provide a transport intervention of N70,000 across all levels for six months, beginning in November 2026. The government also approved peculiar allowance with effect from May 1, 2026, while payment of the arrears is expected to begin in November and will be made in three equal monthly instalments. In addition, the 19 months’ outstanding allowances owed health workers is to be paid within three months, beginning in December 2026. The meeting also agreed that the Minimum Wage Negotiation Committee would be constituted to commence work immediately. However, the parties remained divided over the effective date for implementing the new minimum wage. On the issue of tax relief for workers, the meeting resolved that the matter would be referred to the National Executive Council, as taxation is a statutory issue. Meanwhile, the Federal Ministry of Agriculture and Food Security has submitted the list of beneficiaries and the cost implications of the proposed hazard allowance for agricultural officers to the National Salaries, Incomes and Wages Commission for verification. The verification is expected to be completed within two weeks, after which the commission will issue an implementation template. Similarly, the NSIWC is expected to complete an updated assessment of the cost implications of the proposed CONHESS adjustment within three weeks. The assessment will enable the Presidential Committee on Salaries to take a decision on the matter. The federal government and NLC urged state and local governments to participate in the intervention process and implement the agreed measures. The parties also agreed to reconvene after one month to review the level of implementation of the resolutions. item.title: Tinubu seeks $20.5bn, €1.04bn foreign loans to fund projects
item.description: *Seeks Reps’ approval for ₦269.4bn promissory notes to settle FG’s debts *Senate refers 2026–2027 supplementary borrowing plan to debt committee By Henry Umoru, Luminous Jannamike & Gift Odekina ABUJA — President Bola Tinubu has written the Senate, seeking an approval of a supplementary external borrowing plan of $20.52 billion and €1.045 billion to finance infrastructure and development projects across the country. He also asked the National Assembly to approve establishment and expansion of the Federal Government’s Promissory Note Programme to settle outstanding verified liabilities totalling N269.44 billion. President Tinubu’s letter was addressed to President of the Senate, Senator Godswill Akpabio. Akpabio, who read the letter yesterday at plenary, said the request covered the 2026–2027 fiscal period, targeting critical sectors, including power, transportation, agriculture, healthcare, education, water supply and security. Tinubu, who noted that the proposed borrowing is necessary to bridge Nigeria’s infrastructure funding gap, sustain economic growth, generate employment and improve the living conditions of Nigerians, urged the National Assembly to give the plan urgent consideration and approval to facilitate the timely release of funds and implementation of the projects. In the letter, the president said the proposed external financing will support projects and programmes spanning virtually every sector of the economy. “The 2026–2027 Supplementary External Borrowing Plan cuts across all sectors, with specific emphasis on infrastructure, agriculture, health, education, water supply, growth, security and employment generation, as well as financial management reforms, amongst others,” he said. According to the letter, the proposed facilities cost $20,517,755,901 and €1,045,083,643. It explained that the projects had been selected after technical and economic assessments. “I want to emphasise that the projects and programmes included in the borrowing plan were selected based on thorough technical and economic evaluation, as well as their anticipated contribution to the socio-economic development of the country,” he said. The president, who explained that the proposed investments were expected to create employment opportunities, promote skills acquisition, encourage entrepreneurship, reduce poverty and strengthen food security, said: “These initiatives aim to generate employment, promote skills acquisition, foster entrepreneurship, reduce poverty and enhance food security, all of which improve the livelihood of the Nigerian child.” ‘Loan is for projects in 36 states and FCT’ He disclosed that most of the projects would be executed across the 36 states and the Federal Capital Territory, stressing that the nationwide spread of the interventions would help address development needs across the federation. item.title: Fake drinks may be causing liver, kidney diseases in Ondo — NMA
item.description: By Dayo Johnson, Akure The Ondo State chapter of the Nigerian Medical Association (NMA) has raised the alarm over the circulation of suspected fake and adulterated beverages, warning that they may be contributing to liver and kidney diseases among young people. The association recalled previous incidents involving suspected adulterated drinks in parts of the state in which at least 50 people reportedly died, and called on the Federal Competition and Consumer Protection Commission (FCCPC) and other relevant agencies to intensify efforts to rid the market of counterfeit alcoholic and non-alcoholic beverages. The NMA Chairman in Ondo State, Dr Roland Bola Arohunmolase, raised the concern in Akure while speaking with journalists, saying doctors were encountering liver cirrhosis and kidney disease among younger patients in age groups where such conditions were considered uncommon. He said the association could not yet provide a definitive number of cases linked to suspected adulterated drinks because investigations were ongoing, but described the changing age profile of patients as worrisome. “Traditionally, when you profile some diseases, there are certain age groups in which you do not commonly find them. When a disease no longer conforms to its traditional profile, it becomes a cause for concern,” he said. Arohunmolase said cases of liver cirrhosis among teenagers and liver and kidney diseases among people aged between 22 and 30 required closer medical investigation. “For instance, I don’t expect a child of 15 years or someone between 15 and 18 to develop liver cirrhosis. You begin to wonder why that would happen. Similarly, we are finding liver cirrhosis and kidney disease among young people between the ages of 22 and 30. I think it calls for caution,” he said. The NMA chairman identified the consumption of unhealthy or adulterated beverages as a possible risk factor, while stressing that further investigations were necessary to establish the causes of individual cases. He recalled previous incidents in Odigbo and Irele involving suspected adulterated drinks, which reportedly claimed at least 50 lives, as well as an earlier incident in Ilere linked to methanol consumption. He warned that methanol, an industrial chemical, could cause severe poisoning and organ damage when ingested. According to the association, suspected counterfeit beverages are no longer confined to open markets, as such products have allegedly found their way into supermarkets, hotels, bars and other retail outlets. It warned that beverages produced under unhygienic conditions or made with contaminated water and harmful industrial chemicals could expose consumers to acute poisoning and long-term organ damage. The association called on the FCCPC, the Ondo State Government and other relevant regulatory agencies to conduct aggressive, unannounced inspections of markets, supermarkets, hotels, bars and shops suspected of stocking counterfeit beverages. item.title: Zamfara gets new statistician-general
item.description: Governor Dauda Lawal appointed Kabiru Jelani as the new Statistician-General of Zamfara State. This was contained in a statement signed by the Zamfara State Head of Service, Shehu Baraya. The appointment follows the elevation of the former Statistician-General, Mu’azu Jibril Guraguri, to the position of Permanent Secretary in the state civil service. The statement added that the appointment was to ensure continuity in the leadership of the state’s statistical administration, which plays a critical role in evidence-based policy making, development planning, resource allocation and monitoring of government programmes. The Head of Service urged the appointee to discharge his responsibility with a high sense of professionalism, integrity and dedication to public service. In the same vein, Governor Dauda Lawal has approved the redeployment of 19 Permanent Secretaries across various Ministries, Departments and Agencies in the state civil service. A statement signed by the Zamfara State Head of Service, Alhaji Shehu Baraya, indicates that the redeployment is meant to broaden the administrative experience of the senior public officers, promote cross-sectional knowledge, and strengthen efficiency, accountability and service delivery across the state civil service. The Permanent Secretary, Ministry of Information and Culture, Alhaji Muhammad Salihu Anka has moved to the General Service. item.title: Polio: UNICEF, Zamfara move against disease
item.description: The United Nations Children’s Fund (UNICEF), in collaboration with the Zamfara State Ministry of Information and Culture, organised an awareness walk in Gusau to commemorate World Polio Day. The walk commenced at the Gusau Emir’s Palace and proceeded to Dr. Karima Primary Health Care Centre, Gusau, as part of efforts to raise public awareness about polio prevention, immunisation, and the importance of protecting children against the disease. The initiative highlighted the importance of collaboration between government institutions, development partners, traditional leaders, and communities in the fight against polio and other vaccine-preventable diseases. The awareness walk also serves as a platform to encourage parents and caregivers to ensure that their children receive all recommended doses of the polio vaccine to protect them from lifelong disability caused by the disease. UNICEF and the Zamfara State Ministry of Information and Culture continue to emphasise the importance of public awareness, community participation, and accurate information in promoting immunisation and improving children’s health outcomes across the state. The commemoration reaffirms the collective commitment of stakeholders to supporting polio eradication efforts and ensuring a healthier future for every child in Zamfara State. item.title: 2027: 2.3m electorate to vote in Zamfara
item.description: Governor Dauda Lawal and 19 other governorship candidates would scramble for 2.3 million votes in the February 2027 governorship election in Zamfara state. Governor Lawal, who is seeking reelection under the platform of the All Progressives Congress, will face 19 opposition candidates in the polls. The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) said the state registered voters have risen to 2,265,175 as of August 2026. The figure represents an increase of 313,115 voters, or 16.04 per cent, compared to the 1,952,060 registered voters recorded during the 2023 general elections in the state. The Zamfara INEC Resident Electoral Commissioner, Dr Mahmuda Isah, disclosed this during the election stakeholders’ meeting on the 2027 general elections and PVC collection on Wednesday in Gusau, Zamfara. “I would like to highlight some important electoral statistics that demonstrate both the scale of our responsibilities and the significance of public participation in the electoral process,” Isah said. “The Continuous Voter Registration exercise recorded 313,115 registrations as of August 2026, representing approximately 16.04 per cent of the 2023 registered-voter figure,” he said. He noted that the figures underscore the importance of sustained voter mobilisation, effective public enlightenment and the need to maintain an accurate, credible and inclusive Register of Voters. “Registration records will continue to undergo the necessary verification and validation processes in accordance with the law and approved procedures,” Isah said. According to him, Zamfara comprises 14 Local Government Areas, 147 Registration Areas (Electoral Wards), 3,529 Polling Units, three Senatorial Districts, seven Federal Constituencies and 24 State Assembly Constituencies. “With an average of approximately 553 registered voters per Polling Unit, based on the 2023 figure, these statistics demonstrate the considerable logistical, administrative and security responsibilities involved in conducting elections across the state,” he said. Isah said successful conduct of the 2027 general elections would require meticulous planning, efficient resource deployment, effective security coordination, continuous voter education and active cooperation of all stakeholders. He emphasised that the Permanent Voter Card (PVC) remained an essential requirement for voter accreditation and participation in elections. “The commission, therefore, attaches considerable importance to ensuring that all eligible registered voters have adequate opportunities to collect their PVCs. “Following the conclusion of the ward-level collection exercise, PVC collection will continue at INEC offices in the 14 Local Government Areas of Zamfara, in accordance with the commission’s approved arrangements. “I appeal to all registered voters who are yet to collect their PVCs to visit their respective INEC local government offices and collect their cards personally,” he said. “INEC Zamfara remains resolutely committed to car

item.title: Zamfara steps up Ebola surveillance, screening
item.description: The Zamfara Government had stepped up surveillance against Ebola by conducting mass screening at the Gusau International Airport and across motor parks. This was done to prevent possible spread of the virus in the state. The Commissioner for Health, Dr Nafisa Maradun, disclosed this while flagging-off the response team at the Gusau International Airport on Friday. She said the state government initiated the response measure following the arrival of a passenger, an indigene of Zamfara, from Saudi Arabia via EgyptAir, who presented with high temperature. Maradun said the measures were aimed at preventing an outbreak of the virus in the state. She said the government had also intensified screening of passengers and commuters arriving at Gusau motor parks and other entry points, noting that raising public awareness remained key to curbing possible spread of the virus. The move, according to the commissioner, follows the reported index case in the Federal Capital Territory (FCT), Abuja. The Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention had disclosed that the index patient diagnosed with the Bundibugyo strain of the Ebola virus in Nigeria is a Ugandan-born woman who arrived in the FCT with her husband on October 3. Flagging off the response at the airport, Maradun said: “It becomes necessary as the surveillance team identified a passenger arriving from Saudi Arabia via EgyptAir with high temperature.” She said officials had been deployed to the airport to screen passengers arriving in Zamfara by air to ensure no one imports the Ebola virus into the state. item.title: Governor Lawal repositions health sector, motivates medical workers, improves service delivery — NMA
item.description: Governor Dauda Lawal has been repositioning the healthcare sector in Zamfara state through infrastructural revitalisation, improved healthcare service delivery, institutional strengthening, the Medical Association, (NMA) has said. The NMA Chairman, Zamfara State chapter, Dr Muhammad Murtata Salahu, revealed this at the 2026 Annual Physicians’ Week And Ordinary General Meeting of the association. He reaffirmed the NMA’s readiness to work closely with Governor Lawal’s administration in building a healthcare system that is resilient, accessible, equitable and responsive “A stronger medical profession means a stronger healthcare system, and a stronger healthcare system means a healthier and more prosperous Zamfara,” he said. “On behalf of the entire NMA members in Zamfara let me express our profound appreciation to Governor Dauda Lawal for his visionary leadership, remarkable commitment to healthcare transformation and sustained support for the medical profession. “We acknowledge and commend the determination of the present administration in the state to reposition the healthcare sector through infrastructural revitalisation, improved healthcare service delivery, institutional strengthening and greater attention to the welfare and professional development of healthcare personnel,” he explained. He said. “Governor Dauda Lawal’s commitment of giving the healthcare a priority of his administration demonstrates a clear understanding that a healthy population remains the foundation of sustainable development, economic productivity and social stability. “We particularly appreciate his administration’s responsiveness to the needs and concerns of medical professionals and its efforts towards creating a more conducive environment for effective medical practice. “These initiatives are encouraging and represent important steps towards addressing longstanding challenges within our healthcare system. “The commitment of the state government to healthcare development is commendable, and we assure you of the continued professional support and constructive partnership of the Nigerian Medical Association in translating the state healthcare vision into sustainable benefits for the people of Zamfara. “We equally encourage the governor to sustain this positive momentum through continued investment in healthcare infrastructure, workforce development, improved welfare packages, recruitment and retention of medical personnel, and the strengthening of healthcare services across the state,” he explained. The theme for this year’s Physicians’ Week is, “Securing the Future of Medicine in Nigeria.” Part of the activities marking the week was scientific lectures presentations on polio in Zamfara, Applications of Artificial Intelligence in healthcare, and Diphtheria Case Management. item.title: 4th-tier Fleetwood Town knock Arsenal out of Carabao Cup after penalties
item.description: Arsenal suffered one of the most humiliating defeats in their history as the Premier League champions were stunned by fourth-tier minnows Fleetwood in a League Cup penalty shoot-out on Tuesday. Mikel Arteta’s side crashed out 5-3 on penalties in an incredible fourth round upset after the tie finished 1-1 in normal time. Arsenal’s Bruno Guimaraes had his penalty saved by Jay Lynch in the shoot-out and Conor Haughey scored Fleetwood’s winner. Aaron Loupalo-Bi’s first-half goal had put Fleetwood ahead before Viktor Gyokeres equalised after the interval. Arsenal’s 16-year-old rising star Max Dowman was sent off for violent conduct in the closing stages. Arteta paid the price for prioritising Sunday’s Premier League trip to Liverpool as his decision to make nine changes backfired spectacularly. No one would have predicted Arsenal’s embarrassment regardless of Arteta’s selection gamble. They had moved level on points with Premier League leaders Manchester City after a 2-0 victory over Everton on Saturday. But instead of extending their run of 11 wins from their 13 previous games, Arsenal returned to north London red-faced after a loss that ranks among the darkest days in the club’s glittering history. Referee Michael Salisbury shows a red card to Arsenal’s English midfielder #56 Max Dowman (R) during the English League Cup fourth round football match between Fleetwood Town and Arsenal at Highbury Stadium in Fleetwood, north west England, on October 27, 2026. (Photo by Darren Staples / AFP) Arsene Wenger’s Arsenal suffered a shock League Cup loss against fourth tier Bradford on penalties in 2012. Arteta’s team were beaten by second tier Southampton in the FA Cup last season and also lost to Nottingham Forest, then in the Championship, in the same competition in 2022. Supporters of an older vintage will recall Arsenal’s 1969 League Cup final loss against third tier Swindon and their 1992 FA Cup exit at fourth tier Wrexham. But even those painful defeats cannot compare to this remarkable result. For once, Arsenal fans will not have fond memories of Highbury — Fleetwood’s ground shares the same name as the Gunners’ ancestral home before their move to the Emirates Stadium in 2006. Fleetwood’s tiny 5,327-capacity ground — where goals are celebrated with a burst of children’ cartoon song Captain Pugwash over the tannoy — is a far cry from the famous marble halls and dignified grandeur of Arsenal’s former stadium. Now it will be remembered forever as the site of Arsenal’s most chastening loss in the Arteta era. Fleetwood boss Matt Lawlor wept tears of joy as disbelieving fans flooded the pitch to celebrate their club’s astonishing victory. – ‘Cod Army’ uprising – Only Myles Lewis-Skelly and Viktor Gyokeres kept their places from the Everton game, with teenagers Dowman and Marli Salmon starting, while 18-year-old winger Ceadach O’Neill made his debut. item.title: Former Grand Slam winner Wawrinka ends tennis career
item.description: Stan Wawrinka bid farewell to tennis as he brought the curtain down on a decorated 24-year career following a first-round exit at the Basel Open on Tuesday. The 41-year-old Swiss announced earlier in the season that his last tournament as a professional would be the ATP 500-level event in his home country and a 7-5, 7-6 (7/2) defeat by Czech Jiri Lehecka brought an end to the career of the three-time major champion. Former world number three Wawrinka, along with Andy Murray, was the only player to win multiple Grand Slams in a period dominated by Roger Federer, Rafael Nadal and Novak Djokovic. He bested Nadal to win his first Grand Slam at the Australian Open in 2014, before beating Djokovic in the French Open final the following season and then again in the US Open title-match in 2016. Alongside his compatriot Federer, the Lausanne native won the Davis Cup for Switzerland and claimed gold in the doubles at the 2008 Beijing Olympics. On court in Basel, Wawrinka’s every point won, as well as several trademark booming one-handed backhands, was greeted by wild cheers from the partisan home crowd. But Lehecka got his nose in front with a break of serve in the 11th game and sealed the opening set with an ace as he held to love. A tight second set rumbled towards a tie-break, but it was just a step too far for Wawrinka as his 21st-ranked opponent took firm control to seal the breaker and the match. item.title: Brazil’s Flavio Bolsonaro flees to US after election loss
item.description: Defeated right-wing presidential candidate Flavio Bolsonaro left Brazil and is traveling to the United States despite a court order banning him from exiting the country, US media reported Tuesday. The son of jailed ex-leader Jair Bolsonaro lost elections to incumbent Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva on Sunday and refused to concede defeat. The right-wing senator on Monday said a Supreme Court justice had ordered him to hand over his passports. Bolsonaro is under investigation for alleged corruption and money laundering, and with his election loss is also set to lose his parliamentary immunity. The 45-year-old was heading to Florida, CNN reported Tuesday, citing an anonymous official source. Other US media confirmed he was heading to the country. The US State Department said Tuesday that it would issue visas to Bolsonaro and his family, without confirming his travel plans. A police source told AFP that the senator’s Brazilian and diplomatic passports had been canceled, adding that “there is no formal record of Flavio Bolsonaro leaving the country.” But he has held Italian nationality since 2023, according to an Italian parliamentary document seen by AFP. Bolsonaro’s campaign manager Rogerio Marinho expressed shock over reports that the defeated candidate had fled Brazil. “We still don’t have any news about his whereabouts,” he told reporters in Brasilia on Tuesday. “I received a text message from him this morning, where he said he would let some time pass today and then would talk with us, and that was it,” Marinho said. “That was the only communication we had.” – Scare tactic – Flavio Bolsonaro said Monday that the ban on his exit from Brazil amounted to a scare tactic. “I never had any intention of leaving the country. I will surrender my passports and defend myself against this travesty,” he said in the video posted on Instagram. US President Donald Trump, a close ally of Jair Bolsonaro, on Monday said Brazil’s elections were “rigged” following the defeat of Bolsonaro junior. Flavio’s brother Eduardo, a US-based former lawmaker, maintains close ties with the White House. Last week, he told a US podcast that Flavio Bolsonaro should leave Brazil in the event of electoral defeat, given the active probes into his activities. In his Monday statement, Lula’s challenger also said he would lead the opposition to the leftist government. Following Lula’s victory with 51.8 percent of the vote, Bolsonaro said he would seek to annul the result, citing the decision to extend polling hours over transportation difficulties that prevented some citizens from voting. Lula had requested the extension, as had Bolsonaro over bad weather in parts of the country. – In his father’s footsteps – All bets were on a Bolsonaro win after he came out on top in the first round of elections earlier this month. He campaigned on a pledge to liberate his father, who is under house arrest for coup-plotting after his own electoral loss to Lula in 2022. Jair Bolsonaro never conceded defeat

item.title: FG Approves Six-Month ₦70,000 Transport Support For Workers
item.description: The Federal Government has approved a ₦70,000 transport intervention for workers across all levels for six months, beginning in November 2026, following a conciliation meeting with the leadership of the Nigeria Labour Congress (NLC). The agreement was reached at a meeting convened by the Federal Ministry of Labour and Employment in Abuja on Tuesday, October 27, to address issues raised by organised labour. Under the agreement, the government also approved the payment of peculiar allowance arrears, effective from May 1, 2026, with payments scheduled to begin in November in three equal monthly instalments. The parties, however, failed to agree on the effective date for implementing the national minimum wage, although they agreed that the Minimum Wage Negotiation Committee would be constituted and begin meeting immediately. The resolutions were contained in a press statement issued by the Ministry of Labour and Employment after the meeting, which was chaired by the Minister, Dr Muhammad Maigari Dingyadi, with NLC President Joe Ajaero leading the labour delegation. On the transport intervention, the statement said the Federal Government “will pay a transport intervention of Seventy Thousand Naira (₦70,000) across all levels for a period of six (6) months, commencing from November 2026.” On peculiar allowances, the government approved payments with effect from May 1, 2026, with the arrears to be paid in three equal monthly instalments beginning in November. The verification is expected to be completed within two weeks, after which the commission will issue an implementation template. The parties also discussed the Consolidated Health Salary Structure (CONHESS) adjustment. According to the statement, NSIWC promised to complete the update of the cost implications within three weeks to enable the Presidential Committee on Salaries to decide on the adjustment. item.title: First Israeli Election Exit Polls Show Narrow Edge For Opposition
item.description: The first exit polls from Israel’s elections showed the opposition bloc with a slight edge over Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s camp as voting ended Tuesday, but still shy of an outright majority in the 120-seat Knesset. The country’s main pollsters — Channels 11, 12 and 13 — projected the opposition bloc to win 52 or 53 seats, and Netanyahu’s bloc to win 50, although his Likud would be the largest single party in the parliament, with 24 or 25 seats. Israeli Arab parties also made gains after their voter base turned out in high numbers. The exit polls showed the two Arab-majority groupings, Raam and the Joint List, winning 17 or 18 seats between them. In the last election, Likud had walked away with 32 seats, enabling it to cobble together a coalition with smaller far-right parties after Netanyahu’s traditional allies balked at the corruption cases the premier was facing. This time around, those mainstream right-wing parties, by and large, vowed to work with main challenger Gadi Eisenkot’s Yashar party — projected to nab 21 to 23 seats — to form an opposition coalition capable of unseating Netanyahu. A volunteer stands behind a banner for Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s Likud party at a polling station in Jerusalem on October 27, 2026, on the day of Israel’s legislative election. Photo by Jewel SAMAD / AFP) “The initial exit poll results indicate a complete lack of confidence in Netanyahu and the October 7 government,” Eisenkot said. Israel’s current opposition chief Yair Lapid said Netanyahu’s bloc had suffered a “crushing defeat”, while left-wing leader Yair Golan said the public had “fired the Netanyahu government”. While Raam and the Joint List do not belong to the opposition bloc, they have expressed openness to supporting it. Tuesday’s poll was marked by high turnout, with many voters saying they saw it as pivotal for the country’s future. The following is a party-by-party breakdown of the projected seat count in the first exit polls: Pro-Netanyahu camp Likud, right-wing, led by Benjamin Netanyahu: 24 or 25 Otzma Yehudit, far-right, led by Itamar Ben Gvir: 6 or 7 United Torah Judaism, Ashkenazi ultra-Orthodox, led by Yaakov Asher: 6 or 7 Shas, Sephardic ultra-Orthodox, led by Aryeh Deri: 6 to 8 Religious Zionism, far-right, led by Bezalel Smotrich: 6 Opposition camp Yashar, centrist, led by Gadi Eisenkot: 21 to 23 Beyahad, centre-right, led by Naftali Bennett: 12 to 14 The Democrats, left-wing, led by Yair Golan: 9 or 10 Yisrael Beiteinu, secular right, led by Avigdor Lieberman: 7 to 9 Arab parties Raam, moderate Islamist, led by Mansour Abbas: 7 Joint List, far-left, led by Yousef Jabareen: 10 or 11 The post First Israeli Election Exit Polls Show Narrow Edge For Opposition appeared first on Channels Television .

item.title: We’re not behind waving of Russian flags during 2024 protests in Nigeria – Russia Foreign Minister
item.description: Russian foreign minister Sergey Lavrov has dismissed insinuations that the Russian government sponsored some Nigerian youths who waved Russian flags during the 2024 #EndBadGovernance protests. Lavrov, who spoke in Moscow on the sidelines of the Third Russia-Africa Summit, in response to a question by the News Agency of Nigeria, said Russia had no hand in the action and distanced Moscow from any attempt to undermine Nigeria’s sovereignty. According to him, Russia and Nigeria enjoy a robust relationship dating back to the Soviet Union. He said those who wore Russian flags did so in their personal capacity and that it did not translate into official support from Russia. “Anyone, who donned the Russian flag, did so in his or her personal capacity. It does not mean that Russia was in support of this kind of action. “A lot of citizens sympathetic to Palestinians wave Palestinian flags to express solidarity. It does not mean the Palestinian government is behind them,” Lavrov said. The News Agency of Nigeria(NAN), recalls that the nationwide #EndBadGovernance protests took place from Aug. 1 to Aug. 10, 2024, with the protesters citing high cost of living and economic hardship for their action. NAN also recalls that during the protests, some groups of protesters, mostly youths and minors in Kano, Kaduna, Zamfara and Abuja, were seen waving Russian flags and chanting slogans calling for military intervention. The action, which the Federal Government described as treasonable and a threat to Nigeria’s sovereignty, led to the arrest of scores of protesters and some tailors who were allegedly sewing the flags. The Russian Embassy in Abuja had, at the time, also denied any involvement. Lavrov said the robust relationship between Nigeria and Russia had seen an increase in scholarships awarded to Nigerians, reaching a peak of 220 in 2026. He recalled that in 2024, he met with his Nigerian counterpart in Abuja who warmly received him, and cemented the bilateral ties between the two countries. On defence pacts with some countries in the Sahel, Lavrov said Russia was helping to eliminate security threats in the region, adding that Moscow was aware that some Western capitals were using Ukrainian mercenaries to sabotage the efforts, as they did in Libya, in a bid to undermine regional stability. Commenting on the recent diesel supply agreement with the United States, the foreign minister said it was purely a business decision and would not affect the interest of its allies. “The diesel agreement with the U.S. is purely a business decision by two world leaders who are concerned by the rising cost of energy,” he said. item.title: Sokoto Assembly okays establishment of state police
item.description: The Sokoto State House of Assembly unanimously adopted the Sixth Alteration Bill, which seeks to provide a constitutional framework for establishing state police services in Nigeria. The News Agency of Nigeria reports that the Deputy Majority Leader of the House, Mustapha Abdullahi (APC-Sokoto South II), moved the motionduring plenary in Sokoto on Tuesday. Presenting the bill, Abdullahi said it sought to amend the 1999 Constitution, as altered, to establish state police services while retaining the Nigeria Police Force as the federal police service. He said the executive transmitted the bill, the Senate considered it on June 24, the House of Representatives on July 23, andthe Sokoto Assembly on September 22. According to him, the proposed framework will delineate the responsibilities of federal and state police services to ensure effective policing and address security challenges across the country. He explained that the federal police would handle interstate and international crimes, terrorism, cybercrime, border security, policing of the Federal Capital Territory (FCT) and protection of federal assets. “Conversely, state police services would be responsible for law enforcement, maintenance of public order and safety, protection of lives and property, and investigation of local crimes. “Therefore, the federal police and state police will function side-by-side in every state,” Abdullahi said. The lawmaker added that the federal police could intervene in state policing matters at the request of a state governor or where there was a breakdown of law and order that the state police could not contain. He said the head of a state police service would be known as the State Commander of Police and appointed by the governor on the recommendation of the National Police Council, subject to confirmation by the State House of Assembly. Abdullahi further explained that the bill proposed the establishment of a State Police Service Commission as an executive body responsible for the appointment, promotion and discipline of state police personnel, except the State Commander. On funding, the lawmaker said the proposed framework would provide for the State Police Service Commission to receive funds directly from the state’s Consolidated Revenue Fund to ensure financial autonomy. He added that the Nigeria Police Force would continue to operate in every state until the state’s police service commenced operations. Abdullahi cited Section 9(2) of the 1999 Constitution, as amended, which provides that a constitutional alteration must be approved by resolutions of the houses of assembly of not less than two-thirds of all the states. Contributing to the debate, several lawmakers supported the bill, describing state policing as a necessary measure to address the security challenges confronting states across the country. item.title: ‘What Are You Doing With The Money?’ Umeh Questions Tinubu’s Fresh Loan Request
item.description: The Senator representing Anambra Central, Victor Umeh, has questioned how the Federal Government has spent funds from previous borrowings, asking why budgetary obligations remain unmet despite repeated approvals for loans. Umeh spoke on Channels Television’s Politics Today on Tuesday while reacting to President Bola Tinubu’s request to the National Assembly for approval to borrow an additional $20.5 billion and €1.45 billion. The senator argued that previous borrowing requests were justified on the grounds that the funds would finance government budgets, yet contractors were still owed for capital projects. “The truth is that we have approved so much funds to be borrowed in the past, and on each occasion we’ve been told that this borrowing would be able to fund the budgets and these budgets have remained unfunded up till this day,” Umeh said. ﻿ He noted that three budgets were running concurrently, while the government had yet to meet its obligations to contractors handling capital projects. “Three budgets are running concurrently and the government is not meeting its obligations to contractors on capital projects and so on and so forth. So if you borrow to finance a budget and you are not able to finance that budget, where has the money gone to? That is the question in the lips of everybody,” he said. Umeh also suggested that the latest loan request would eventually receive legislative approval, arguing that opposition lawmakers would be outvoted by members of the ruling party. President Tinubu has written to the National Assembly seeking approval for the Federal Government’s 2026–2027 supplementary external borrowing plan, valued at $20.5 billion and €1.45 billion. The government says the proposed loans would fund critical infrastructure, agriculture, education and other key sectors of the economy in line with the administration’s development priorities. The request has added to the debate over the government’s borrowing plans and Nigeria’s rising debt burden. item.title: South-East monarchs renew demand for Nnamdi Kanu’s release
item.description: — Insist on leadership rotation to Abia, urge massive voter turnout By Steve Oko The South-East Traditional Rulers Council has renewed its demand for the unconditional release of detained Indigenous People of Biafra, IPOB, leader, Mazi Nnamdi Kanu, lamenting that previous appeals to the Federal Government have failed to yield the desired outcome. The monarchs also reaffirmed their position that the council’s leadership should rotate to Abia State, with HRM Eze Sir Dr Linus Nto Mbah assuming the chairmanship in accordance with the council’s constitution. These resolutions were contained in a communiqué issued after the council’s quarterly delegates meeting held on October 23, 2026, at the Parliament of Ndi Eze, Owerri, Imo State. On the political front, the traditional rulers expressed concern over the scheduled dates for the forthcoming national elections, which they said could pose challenges for the South-East. They nevertheless urged eligible voters across the region to return to their respective registration areas and participate massively in the elections. The council also called on traditional rulers and community leaders to suspend festivals and ceremonies during the election period to enable eligible voters to exercise their civic responsibilities. On traditional leadership in the South, the monarchs reaffirmed their support for the rotational chairmanship of the Southern Traditional Rulers Council among the South-East, South-West and South-South geopolitical zones. They rejected any arrangement that would confer permanent chairmanship on one zone, insisting that the position should rotate among the three zones for two-year terms, in line with the decision of the Southern Governors Forum reached in Ogun State in 2025. The council further called for the reconstitution of the Southern Traditional Rulers Council’s leadership to reflect recognised traditional rulers from member states and conform to the leadership template of the Southern Governors Forum. The communiqué was signed by the chairman of the South-East Traditional Rulers Council and chairman of the Abia State Council of Traditional Rulers, HRM Eze Dr Linus Nto Mbah; the Obi of Onitsha, HRM Igwe Nnaemeka Achebe; and other traditional rulers from the five South-East states. The monarchs expressed appreciation to Imo State Governor, Senator Hope Uzodimma, for hosting the meeting, as well as the Imo State Council of Traditional Rulers and the people of the state for their hospitality. They also acknowledged the support and encouragement of governors across the South-East. The post South-East monarchs renew demand for Nnamdi Kanu’s release appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: 2027: How we will curb election violence – INEC
item.description: .Vows to hunt down anyone who threatens ad-hoc staff, corps members .Set to hold National Election Security Confab By Omeiza Ajayi ABUJA: The Independent National Electoral Commission INEC has unveiled an intelligence-led security framework to curb violence ahead of the 2027 General Election, vowing to hunt down anyone who threatens its ad-hoc staff, National Youth Service Corps NYSC members or permanent personnel. INEC Chairman, Prof. Joash Amupitan SAN, disclosed this in Gombe on Tuesday while declaring open the North-East Zonal Interactive Meeting with Staff and Readiness Assessment for the 2027 General Election. The Commission in its daily bulletin said it was shifting from reactive, election-day deployments to a framework designed to protect voters, personnel and electoral materials before any ballot paper is moved. INEC said its collaboration with the Nigeria Police Force, the Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps NSCDC, the Department of State Services DSS, the Armed Forces and other paramilitary agencies under the Inter-Agency Consultative Committee on Election Security ICCES has, according to him, been fundamentally restructured. The new framework, which the Commission terms the “ICCES Tentacle,” extends inter-agency security coordination from national and state headquarters directly down to the most remote Local Government Areas and Registration Area Centres. Amupitan told the gathering that no election, however well planned administratively, could be deemed credible if voters, election personnel and observers operate under physical threat or fear of violence. He explained that the framework rests on three pillars, the first being “Map and Mitigate.” Under it, the Commission will use Electoral Risk Management (ERM) tools to identify security flashpoints, seasonal threat factors and local vulnerabilities early, so that security agencies can deploy proactive measures long before ballot papers arrive. The second pillar, “Ensure Safety,” provides a protective umbrella over all electoral personnel, technological assets, including Bimodal Voter Accreditation System (BVAS) devices and server infrastructure, and, most importantly, the voter. The third pillar, “Guarantee Access,” is aimed at ensuring that each of the 176,846 polling units nationwide remains a safe, peaceful and dignified space for the exercise of democratic rights, regardless of geographical remoteness or historical security challenges. According to him, the collaboration among the agencies had already produced concrete results. He disclosed that joint operations led by the DSS recently uncovered a covert plot by criminal kingpins targeting the Commission’s ad-hoc staff and Youth Corps members. item.title: Tinubu’s Difficult Reforms Beginning To Bear Fruit, Says Adesina
item.description: Former African Development Bank (AfDB) President Akinwunmi Adesina has said President Bola Tinubu’s economic reforms are beginning to yield results, citing increased foreign exchange availability, renewed portfolio investments and a downward trend in inflation. Adesina, who visited Tinubu on Tuesday, described the removal of the petrol subsidy and the harmonisation of exchange rate windows as “very important, difficult reforms”, adding that the government must now focus on translating economic stabilisation into growth and prosperity. Speaking to State House correspondents after the meeting, the former AfDB chief said Nigeria’s international perception had also improved, pointing to the outlooks assigned to the country by rating agencies. “If you look at it, you have a lot more FX available today. You have a lot of portfolio investors that are coming into the country. You have inflation trending downwards. Prices are still a bit high, but inflation is trending downwards,” he said. ﻿ Adesina added that some rating agencies had given Nigeria stable or positive outlooks, describing the development as an indication of changing perceptions of the country. He, however, said the gains from the reforms should be followed by a stronger focus on structural transformation and economic expansion. “Now that’s just the beginning of the work. I think the most critical thing is the president realised this, and everybody knows that being a dentist is not a very difficult job. But you have to also now move from the issue of the reforms and stabilisation, straight into structural transformation and also growth and prosperity, which is what the president is focusing on,” he said. Adesina also expressed his willingness to contribute to Nigeria’s development in any capacity the President considers appropriate, insisting that he was not seeking a political appointment. “I told the President, I’m back at home, here to help and ready to help. It’s my country. I love my country, and I’m ready to help,” he said. Asked in what capacity he could support Nigeria, given his experience on the international stage, Adesina said he was prepared to serve wherever his contribution would be useful. “I’m fully able to help Nigeria in any capacity. I’ve always had that. You know, my heart is always at home. And in any capacity that His Excellency feels I can help, I can help in anything. I’m not looking for a job. I’m not looking for anything. I’m just here to help,” he said. “It’s my country. I have a duty, an obligation, and a responsibility to do so, and I will.” Adesina also briefed Tinubu on his 10-year tenure as AfDB president, which ended after two terms, and the bank’s support for Nigeria during that period. He said the AfDB provided about $7 billion in financing to Nigeria between 2015 and 2025, compared with $11.1 billion in total financing since the bank began operations in the country in 1971. “So, within 10 years, we were able to do 63 percent, literally, of that,” he said
